t.hero.title: Our treatments
t.hero.lede: Consultation-led care for piles, fissure, fistula and other anorectal problems — first the examination, then the right treatment path for your condition.
t.approach.title: Consultation first — then the treatment decision
t.approach.p1: Treatment begins with a consultation and an examination. The same symptom can have more than one cause, so the condition is assessed before any treatment decision. After the examination, the doctor explains what is going on and the paths available to you.
t.approach.p2: In general the path runs: conservative care and medicines first, where appropriate; simple office procedures if needed; and surgery — only when it is truly required.
t.approach.h1d: Easing constipation, more fibre and fluids, warm baths and, when needed, creams or medicines — in many cases symptoms improve with these first steps alone.
t.approach.h2d: When home care is not enough, certain procedures (such as banding or injections) can help — many of these can be done without hospital admission.
t.approach.h3d: Not every problem needs surgery. When a condition is large, long-standing or complex, the doctor explains the surgical options and their risks before advising.
t.approach.p3: Where applicable, many procedures can be done without hospital admission — what your own case needs is explained after the examination. The clinic works with modern treatment methods, and the right path is chosen according to the findings and your condition.

t.cond.title: Conditions we treat
t.cond.lede: Each condition page covers what it is, symptoms, causes, when to see a doctor and the treatment options.
t.cond.piles.d: Blood, itching, pain or a lump during bowel movements — care runs from home treatment to office procedures, depending on the type and severity.
t.cond.fissure.d: A sudden sharp or burning pain when passing stool — home care, medicines or a procedure may be needed for the tear to heal.
t.cond.fistula.d: Repeated pus discharge, pain and swelling near the anus — a fistula usually does not settle on its own, so evaluation matters.
t.cond.other.d: Itching, a lump, constipation or bleeding — come in for an examination and consultation to find the cause.
